subject: Proposal: epoch-weighted p50/p95 commitments for Hosted API
messages:
From: Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@finwell.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question: latency commitments for pilot contract

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked very promising. Before we move to procurement, Procurement and Engineering have one ask: can Redwood propose an approach to p50/p95 commitments that handles short high-traffic epochs (e.g., batch processing at night) without inflating reported p95 during those spikes? Finwell needs a commitment that tracks normal interactive traffic while carving out brief heavy-load epochs where our batch jobs run.

Two quick clarifications we need:
- How would the SLO be measured (windowing / sample weighting)?
- What evidence would you provide for compliance and for exception handling?

Can you send an initial suggestion this week? Procurement is on a tight timetable.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Sanders
Head of Platform Engineering
Finwell Health

Attachment: none
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@finwell.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: latency commitments for pilot contract

Hi Tim — really appreciate the follow-up and the clear ask.

High level proposal (summary):
- Measure p50/p95 on interactive traffic only (requests tagged by client API key and traffic-type routing).
- Define "epochs" as any contiguous 30-minute interval where request rate exceeds the 99th percentile of historical per-minute load for that client. Epochs are excluded from p95 calculation if they meet the carveout criteria below.
- Carveout criteria: epochs where >60% of requests are identified as non-interactive (batch/async) OR where median payload size > X KB.
- For transparency, we provide per-epoch export CSVs and an annotated timeline highlighting excluded windows. Exceptions must be raised within 5 business days after the epoch to be considered for exclusion.

I attached a short draft describing the epoch-weighted approach and a sample measurement export. This is intentionally conservative; if Finwell prefers tighter bounds (shorter epoch length or lower threshold) we can adjust.

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement reviews the draft and confirms acceptability of the 30-minute epoch definition.
2) We run a 2-week telemetry export of your test API key so we can recommend tuned thresholds.
3) Launch pilot with the agreed carveout rules; finalize contractual language if pilot metrics match expectations.

Looping in Kimberly for legal/pricing implications on carveouts (cc). Lauren — can you advise if this changes our committed unit pricing for the pilot?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Solutions (Sales)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-epoch-slo-draft.pdf (7 pages)
From: Jill Park <jill.park@finwell.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: latency commitments for pilot contract

Aditya — this looks like a good starting point. A few comments from Procurement/Legal:
- Procurement wants the epoch detection algorithm to be deterministic and auditable; can Redwood commit to publishing the detection logic and the raw per-minute load used to compute the 99th percentile for our account?
- Legal: exception windows should have a maximum cumulative carveout of 1.5% of measurement time per quarter (we don't want open-ended exclusions).
- Ops: during an excluded epoch, what is the fallback behavior? If you route to a lower-cost region/model are we notified and does that count as a service-level failure for availability?

If you can annotate the draft with those points and send updated language, we can try to get sign-off from Procurement by Friday.

Thanks,
Jill Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Finwell Health

Attachment: finwell-feedback-annotated.docx (comments inline)
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@finwell.com>, Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@finwell.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: latency commitments for pilot contract

Thanks Jill — good points. Quick responses inline below and I've attached an annotated version of the draft: redwood-epoch-slo-draft.pdf (v2).

- Deterministic detection: we can publish the detection algorithm (pseudo-code + parameters) and include an account-specific per-minute rate CSV so Finwell can reproduce the epoch identification. We will ship the CSV for the pilot telemetry export.
- Cumulative carveout cap: 1.5% per quarter is reasonable; we'll add that as a contractual cap but with a "good faith" review clause if we see systematic differences.
- Fallback behavior: during excluded epochs we will not count degraded latency against the SLO; however, we will still report any model downgrade or cross-region fallback as an event in the timeline. Service is considered available unless the HTTP status is 5xx for >1 minute continuous — availability SLA remains unchanged. We'll add explicit wording to clarify that routing fallbacks don't automatically trigger an SLA failure.

Lauren and Markus: does the carveout cap or the deterministic export requirement change the pricing or support commitments for the pilot? If so, please advise and we'll present a single redline to Finwell.

Best,
Aditya

Attachment: redwood-epoch-slo-draft.pdf (v2, 8 pages); slo-measurement-sample.csv
